title: INVITE GOD TO RENEW YOUR MIND AND PURIFY YOUR HEART
text: Glory to God. Glory to God. Hallelujah. We give you praise, Lord Jesus. We bless your holy name this morning. Father, we thank you. We thank you for the gift of this day. We thank you because your mercies are new every morning and great is your faithfulness. I want you to lift your hands wherever you are this morning and just breathe a word of thanksgiving to the Father. Just tell him, "Lord, I am grateful. I am grateful that you woke me up. I am grateful that you preserved me through the night. I am grateful that [music] your hand is still upon my life. Hallelujah." Before we go any further, I want you to share this prayer with someone this morning. Share it with a brother. Share it with a sister. Share it with a friend who needs to encounter the living God today. Because what God is about to do in this place, in this atmosphere, is not for one person alone. The [music] spirit of God is moving and he wants to move through you to reach somebody else. So, please, right now, before we even go into this ministration, share this. Send it to someone. Let the word go. Let the fire spread. Hallelujah. Now, settle your heart. Settle your spirit. I want you to be present with me [music] this morning. Not just physically, not just with your eyes, but with your spirit. Because what we about to encounter is not an ordinary service. This is a divine appointment. God arranged for you to be here this morning. He did not make a mistake when he allowed you to see this. You are here because heaven scheduled you to be here. And by the time we are done this morning, you will not leave the same. You will not leave the same. Something is going to shift in your inner man. Something is going to change in the architecture of your mind and the landscape of your heart. Glory to God. Let me read to you from the book of Romans chapter 12, verse 2. Paul says, and I want you to receive this not as the words of a man, but as the breath of the living God. He says, "And be not conformed to this world, but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind that you may prove what is that good and acceptable and perfect will of God. Hallelujah. And then I want to take you to Psalm 51:10 where David cried out from the depths of his brokenness and said create in me a clean heart oh God and renew a right spirit within me. Two cries two divine imperatives, the renewing of the mind and the purifying of the heart. And this morning these two realities are going to become your portion in the name of Jesus Christ. Hallelujah. Now I want you to understand something fundamental before we proceed. Many believers are struggling not because God has abandoned them, not because the anointing is not real not because the covenant is not in force. They are struggling because the battlefield has never been properly addressed. And where is the battlefield? The battlefield is the mind. The Apostle Paul in 2 Corinthians chapter 10 verses 3 through 5 said that the weapons of our warfare are not carnal but they are mighty through God to the pulling down of strongholds casting down imaginations and every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God and bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ. Did you see that? He said bringing every thought into captivity. That means thoughts can be prisoners, thoughts can be fugitives, thoughts can be rebels. And unless you take authority over your thought life, you will live a life that is far beneath your divine inheritance. Hallelujah. You see, when God saved you, he did not only save your spirit. Salvation is a comprehensive redemption. It is the redemption of your spirit, the redemption of your soul and ultimately the redemption of your body. But here is where many people miss it. When you gave your life to Jesus Christ, your spirit was instantaneously regenerated. Second Corinthians 5:17 says, "Therefore, if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature. Old things are passed away. Behold, all things are become new." That is the spirit. The spirit became new, but the mind The mind does not become new automatically. The mind has to be deliberately, intentionally, consistently renewed. The mind is like a garden. If you do not tend to it, if you do not cultivate it, if you do not remove the weeds, the garden will grow things that you never planted and never intended to harvest. And this is the condition of many believers today. They have a regenerated spirit living inside a mind that has never been renewed, and so there is a war. There is a civil war happening on the inside. The spirit is crying one thing, and the mind is screaming another thing. The spirit is saying you are healed, and the mind is saying you cannot possibly be healed. The spirit is saying you are more than a conqueror, and the mind is saying, "Look at your circumstances. Look at your past. Look at your failures. Look at your limitations." And because the mind has been conditioned by the world, by trauma, by disappointment, by the lies of the enemy, by wrong associations, by wrong information, the mind keeps winning the argument. And the believer lives in defeat not because they lack the spirit of God, but because they have never allowed the spirit of God to go to [music] work on their mind. Hallelujah. This is why Paul says, "Be ye transformed." The Greek word there is metamorpho, from which we get the English word metamorphosis. He's not talking about an adjustment. He's not talking about a minor modification. He's talking about a complete transformation. A caterpillar does not just get a makeover to become a butterfly. It goes through a complete internal overhaul. Everything about it changes. And that is what God wants to do with your mind this morning. He wants to so completely transform the way you think that what comes out of your life, your decisions, your words, your reactions, your relationships, your capacity to receive and operate in the supernatural is utterly different from what it was before because your life will always move in the direction of your most dominant thoughts. Let me say that again. Your life will always move in the direction of your most dominant thoughts. Proverbs 23:7 [music] says, "For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he." If your thoughts are broken, your life will be broken. If your thoughts are small, your life will be small. If your thoughts are contaminated, your life will produce contamination. But if your mind is renewed by the word and the spirit of God, if the thoughts you entertain are thoughts that are consistent with what heaven says about you, then your life will begin to align with the will of God >> [music] >> and you will start to experience things that people around you cannot explain. Hallelujah. Now, let us talk about the heart because this is the second dimension of what God is doing this morning. The mind and the heart. And when I use the word heart here, I'm using it in the biblical sense. I am talking about the seat of your emotions, your will, your desires, your affections, your motivations. Jesus said in Matthew 5:8, "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God." He did not say blessed are the intelligent. He did not say blessed are the gifted. He did not say blessed are those who have read the most books. He said blessed are the pure in heart. Why? [music] Because purity of heart determines the clarity of your spiritual vision. And spiritual vision determines the quality of your walk with God. If your heart is cluttered with offenses, with unforgiveness, with secret sins, with compromise, with divided loyalties, your spiritual vision becomes blurry. You start to see God through the distorted lens of your unresolved heart issues. And that affects how you [music] pray, how you worship, how you receive from God, how you relate to His word, how you respond to His voice. Hallelujah. David understood this. David, after his great failure, after the Bathsheba incident, after everything had collapsed around him, after Nathan the prophet had exposed him, David did not run from God. David ran to God. And when he ran to God, he did not run with excuses, he did not run with justifications, he ran with brokenness, he ran with transparency. And in Psalm 51, he prayed one of the most powerful prayers in all of scripture. He said, "Create in me a clean heart, oh God." He used the word create, bara, in Hebrew, the same word used in Genesis 1:1, when God [music] created the heavens and the earth. He was saying, "God, this is not a renovation job. This is not a paint over job. This needs to be a creative act of your power. I need you to reach into the depths of who I am [music] and create something that was not there before. I need something brand new. I need purity that only you can produce." And God answered that prayer. And God is going to answer it for you this morning. God is going to answer it for you this morning. Hallelujah. Now, here is something I need you to understand about heart purity and why it matters so urgently in this season. We are living in a time of increasing spiritual activity on both sides. The kingdom of light and the kingdom of darkness are both moving with unprecedented intensity. And in this season, God is looking for vessels. He is not LOOKING FOR PERFECT PEOPLE, he's looking for pure people. He's not looking for the most talented, he's looking for those whose hearts are fully His. Second Chronicles 16:9 says, "For the eyes of the Lord run to and fro throughout the whole earth to show himself strong in the behalf of them [music] whose heart is perfect toward him." God is searching. God is scanning the earth right now, and he's not scanning for credentials, he's scanning for hearts. He's looking for someone whose heart is turned completely toward him. And when he finds that person, he shows himself strong on their behalf. He becomes their defense. He becomes their provider. He becomes their strength. He becomes their breakthrough. So, the question this morning is not whether God is willing, the question is is your heart positioned? Is your heart clean enough to be a landing strip for the glory of God? Hallelujah. So, how does this renewal happen? How does the mind get renewed and the heart get purified? I want to take you through this because understanding the process is as important as desiring the outcome. The first agent of renewal is the word of God. Jesus said in John 17:17, "Sanctify them through thy truth. Thy word is truth." The word of God is not merely information, it is a living, active, supernatural force. Hebrews 4:12 says, "For the word of God is quick and powerful and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit and of the joints and marrow and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart." The word of God has the ability to penetrate places that no human counselor can reach. It goes beyond your conscious mind into the subconscious. It goes beyond your surface emotions into the deep motivations of your heart. And as you expose yourself consistently daily, hungrily to the word of God, it begins to displace the lies. It begins to uproot the wrong patterns of thinking. It begins to rewire the neural pathways of your soul. And this is not mysticism, this is a spiritual reality that even science is beginning to confirm. Neuroplasticity, the brain's capacity to rewire itself, is a natural reflection of the spiritual truth that God established before science even had a language for it. That the mind can be renewed, that you are not a prisoner of your past, that you are not forever defined by what you were before. Hallelujah. The second agent of renewal is the Holy Spirit. Romans 8:26 says that the spirit helps our infirmities, and one of our greatest infirmities is the infirmity of a darkened mind and a hardened heart. When you yield yourself to the Holy Spirit, when you give him permission to work, when you surrender your thought life to him, when you ask him to search you as David asked in Psalm 139:23, "Search me, oh God, and know my heart. Try me and know my thoughts." The Holy Spirit goes to work like a divine surgeon. He puts his finger on the things that are wrong. He shines his light in the dark corners of your inner life. And he does not expose those things to condemn you. He exposes them to heal you. He exposes them to free you. The Holy Spirit is not a harsh inspector, he's a loving physician. And when he puts his finger on a wound, it is because he wants to heal it, not because he wants to humiliate you. So, this morning, as we go into prayer, I want you to give the Holy Spirit full permission, full access, not partial, not selective, full access to your mind and to your heart, and watch what he does. Hallelujah. The third agent is prayer itself. There is a dimension of mind renewal and heart purification that only happens in the place of sustained, intentional, passionate prayer. When you pray in the spirit, when you pray in tongues as the Holy Ghost gives utterance, you are praying in a language that bypasses your natural mind and operates directly in the realm of the spirit. Paul said in 1 Corinthians 14:14, "For if I pray in an unknown tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful." And some people read that and they think it is a disadvantage. No, it is a profound advantage because there are things your natural mind does not know how to pray for. There are depths of need in your inner man that your English or your Hausa or your Yoruba or whatever language you speak cannot adequately express. But when you pray in the spirit, your spirit connects with the Holy Spirit and together they make intercession for needs that are too deep for words. And in that transaction, something happens in your mind. Something happens in your heart. You come out of extended prayer in tongues and you find that the anxiety is gone. You find that the confusion is lifted. You find that the burden has been replaced with a peace that passes all understanding [music] because the spirit of God has been working on your inner man while your spirit prayed. Hallelujah. Now, I want to speak prophetically for a moment because the Holy Spirit is moving and I need to be obedient to what he's saying. There is someone watching this morning and you have been carrying a wound in your mind, a wound that came from what someone said to you. Words that were spoken over you in childhood. Words that defined you negatively. Words that told you that you were not enough. Words that told you that you were a mistake. Words that told you that you would never amount to anything. And those words took root in your mind and they became a lens through which you have interpreted every experience ever since. And when God tries to speak to you about your destiny, when he tries to tell you who you really are, when he tries to show you the greatness he deposited inside you, your mind filters that divine communication through this old wound and rejects it. But I declare to you this morning by the authority of the name of Jesus Christ, that wound is being healed today. That lie is being uprooted today. The The voice of the father is louder than the voice of your past. The word of God is more authoritative than any word that any human being has ever spoken over your life. And I prophetically declare, receive your mind back. Receive your mind back in the name of Jesus. Hallelujah. There is also someone else watching and you have been dealing with impurity of heart, not necessarily what the world would call major sin, but a slow drift, a gradual cooling of your affection for God. A creeping compromise. A subtle double-mindedness where you love God, but you also love other things with an equal passion. And God has been nudging you, he has been knocking. He has been sending signals through messages, through people, through circumstances, and this morning is not a coincidence. This is God's final loving appeal to your heart before this season closes. And he's saying, [music] "Come back." Not with condemnation. Not with an ultimatum of harsh judgment. He's saying with outstretched arms, "Come back. Let me purify your heart. Let me renew your first love." Revelation 2:2-5, Jesus said to the church at Ephesus, "Nevertheless, I have somewhat against thee because thou has left thy first love." "Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen and repent and do the first works. Come back to the first works. Come back to the place of passion. Come back to the place where God was not just a part of your life, he was your life. Come back." Hallelujah. I want to also speak to the intercessors, the prophets, the those who carry a burden for this generation. Some of you have been in spiritual battle for so long that you yourself have become weary and your own inner life has been neglected. You have been pouring out for others, but you have not allowed God to pour back into you. You have been strong for everyone around you, but on the inside you are dry, you are exhausted, your mind is tired. And God is saying this morning, let me minister to you. Let me come to where you are. The way the angel came to Elijah under the juniper tree, 1 Kings 19, the angel did not preach to Elijah, the angel did not rebuke Elijah. The angel touched him and said, "Arise and eat, because the journey is too great for thee." God is saying the journey ahead of you is too great for you to go on the way you are. You need to be renewed. You need to be refueled. [music] You need to allow the Lord your God to do something fresh in [music] your inner man. And as we go into this prayer this morning, let this be your moment. Let this be your moment of divine refreshing. Hallelujah. I want to also address the young people, the young men and young women who are in the battle of the mind in a very particular way. You are living in the most information-saturated, image-saturated, thought-saturated generation that has ever existed on the planet. Every day you are bombarded with thousands of images, thousands of messages, thousands of narratives, and many of them are directly contrary to the kingdom of God. And the enemy knows that if he can capture the mind of a generation, he can determine the destiny of a generation. This is not a natural battle. Paul said in Ephesians 6:12, "For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, [music] against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places." There is a principality whose assignment is to colonize the minds of the young, to fill their imagination with corruption, [music] to normalize perversion, to make them comfortable with compromise. And the only answer, the only real, lasting, effective answer is the renewing of the mind by the spirit and word of God. Romans 12:2 is not just a nice theological concept. It is survival [music] strategy for this generation. Be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind. Hallelujah. Now, let us talk about what a renewed mind actually looks like in practical experience because I do not want to leave this in the realm of the abstract. A renewed mind thinks differently about God. Instead of seeing God as distant, judgemental, or disinterested, a renewed mind perceives God as the loving father that he is. Romans 8:15 says, "For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear, but ye have received the spirit of adoption whereby we cry Abba, Father." Abba, the Aramaic word for Daddy, intimacy, access, confidence in the presence of God. That is what a renewed mind produces in your relationship with the Father. A renewed mind also thinks differently about itself. Not with arrogance, not with pride, but with a settled confidence in what God has said. Not what your background says, not what your failure say, not what the enemy whispers, but what God declares in His word. Jeremiah 29:11, "For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the Lord, thoughts of peace and not of [music] evil, to give you an expected end." A renewed mind rests in that. A renewed mind says, "I do not have to earn God's favor because His thoughts toward me are already good. I do not have to perform for His love because His love is unconditional. I do not have to be afraid of tomorrow because He has already been there and He has made provision." Hallelujah. A renewed mind also thinks differently about other people. One of the most devastating effects of an unrenewed mind is how it makes you relate to people around you. An unrenewed mind is suspicious, competitive, envious, easily offended, quick to judge, but a mind that has been saturated with the love of God begins to see people the way God sees them. It sees potential, it sees value, it sees the image of God in every human being regardless of how broken they appear on the outside. And this transformation in how you think about people transforms your relationships, your ministry, your ability to love as Christ commanded us to love. John 13:35, By [music] this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another. The evidence of a renewed mind and a purified heart is love, real love. Sacrificial love, inconvenient love, the kind of love that costs you something. Hallelujah. A renewed mind thinks differently about circumstances. When you face trials, when you face opposition, when you face delays and setbacks and disappointments, an unrenewed mind immediately goes to the worst possible interpretation. God has forgotten me. God does not care. This is the end. This is a punishment. I will never recover from this. But a renewed mind says what James 1 says, My brethren, Count it all joy when you fall into divers temptations, knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. A renewed mind says this is not the end. This is the furnace. And the purpose of the furnace is not my destruction, it is my purification. Job said in Job 23:10, But he knoweth the way that I take. When he had tried me, I shall come forth [music] as gold. A renewed mind does not see the trial as a punishment from a God who is angry. He sees the trial as a process in the hands of a God who is working everything for my good. Romans 8:28, And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose. Hallelujah. Now, let us begin to move into the place of prayer because that is where the real work is going to happen this morning. I want you to understand that everything I have been saying is not just teaching for the sake of information. It is preparation for encounter. The reason I've been laying this word is because faith comes by hearing and hearing by the word of God. And before you can receive from God, you need to know what he is willing and ready to do. You need to know what is available. You need to know what he has promised. And now that you know, now that you have heard, it is time to ask. It is time to seek. It is time to knock. Matthew 7:7, "Ask and it shall be given you. Seek and you shall find. Knock and it shall be opened unto you." So, let us go before [music] the throne of grace with boldness as Hebrews 4:16 says. Not timidly, not with shame, not with a sense that we are unworthy to approach. The blood of [music] Jesus Christ has given us access. The blood has opened the door. The blood has made a way. And we are coming this morning not in our own righteousness, but in the righteousness of Jesus Christ, covered in his blood, standing on his word, and believing for his power to move in our inner man. Hallelujah. Lift your hands right now. Lift your hands wherever you are. You can be in your room, you can be in your car, you can be in your office, you can be anywhere, but lift your hands as an act of surrender. As a declaration that you are opening yourself to God. That you are not coming with resistance. [music] That you are not coming with excuses. That you are coming with a yielded heart and a surrendered mind. And I want you to begin to pray with me right now. Open your mouth. Speak from your spirit. Let your prayer be real and let your prayer be urgent [music] because this is not a casual moment. This is a moment of divine encounter. Let us pray. Father, in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, we come before your throne this morning. We come [music] with thanksgiving in our hearts and praise on our lips. We bless you, Lord, for who you are. We bless you because you are the God who heals and restores and renews. We bless you because you are the God who does not give up on broken things. You are the God who looks at what the enemy has shattered and says, "I will rebuild. I will restore. I will renew." And we bless you this morning for that nature, for that character, for that faithfulness. Hallelujah. Glory to your name. Father, we come this morning with a specific request. Lord, invade our minds. We're inviting you. We're giving you deliberate, conscious, willing permission to enter the territory of our minds. Lord, you said in Revelation 3:20, "Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If any man hear my voice and open the door, I will [music] come in to him." We are opening the door this morning. We are opening the door of our minds. We are opening the door of our thoughts. We are opening the door of our imaginations. Come in, Lord. Come in as the spirit of wisdom and revelation, as Ephesians 1:17 describes. Come in as the spirit of truth, as John 14:17 describes. Come in and evict everything that does not belong. Come in and renovate. Come in and renew. We yield our minds to you right now, Father, in Jesus' name. Hallelujah. Every thought pattern that was formed in our minds by the world, by the enemy, by traumatic experiences, by the lies that were spoken over us, we renounce those patterns right now. By the power and authority in the blood of Jesus Christ, we cast down imaginations, as 2 Corinthians 10:2-5 commands. We cast down every high thing that has exalted itself above the knowledge of God in our minds. Every lie that said we are worthless, we cast it down. Every lie that said God cannot use us, we cast it down. Every lie that said our situation is permanent, we cast it [music] down. Every lie that said the best days are behind us, we cast it down. In the name of Jesus, we pull down those strongholds right now. We pull them down by the blood of the lamb and the word of our testimony. Revelation 12:11, "They overcame by the blood of the lamb." We overcome these mental strongholds by the blood of the lamb this morning. Fire of God, fall. Fire of the Holy Ghost fall on every mind. Burn the chaff. Burn the debris. Burn the contamination. Fire of God fall in the name of Jesus. Hallelujah. And now Father, we ask you to release the spirit of revelation over our minds. Ephesians 1:18, let the eyes of our understanding be enlightened. Lord, we do not want to just know about you academically. We want to know you experientially. We want to see you clearly. We want to think your thoughts after you. Lord, let the mind of Christ be our portion this morning. 1 Corinthians 2:16, for who hath known the mind of the Lord that he may instruct him. But we have the mind of Christ. We have the mind of Christ. We receive the mind of Christ by faith this morning. We declare our minds are being renewed. Our minds are being transformed. Our minds are being brought into alignment with the will of heaven. What God thinks about our lives, we receive as our reality. What the word declares about our identity, we embrace [music] as our truth. We are the righteousness of God in Christ Jesus. We are seated with Christ in heavenly places. We are more than conquerors through him who loved us. We are the apple of God's eye. We are fearfully and wonderfully made. We are chosen, royal, holy, God's own special possession as 1 Peter 2:2-9 declares. We receive these truths not just as nice scriptures, but as the foundation of our thinking from this day forward in Jesus name. Hallelujah. Now we go deeper. We go to the level of the heart. Father, we come before you the way David came with boldness born of desperation. Create in us a clean heart, oh God. As you created the heavens and the earth in Genesis [music] 1, reach into the depths of who we are and create what was not there before. Create purity where there has been contamination. Create passion where there has been coldness. Create love where there has been bitterness. Create faith where there has been unbelief. Create courage where there has been fear. Create generosity where there has been selfishness. Create a heart that is fully, completely, unreservedly yours. We pray this prayer as the cry of our souls this morning. Create in us a clean heart, oh God. Hallelujah. Let the blood of Jesus Christ, [music] that powerful, potent, eternally effective blood, let it do its cleansing work right now. 1 John 1 - 7 says, "The blood of Jesus Christ, His Son, cleanseth us from all sin." Not some sin, all sin. Not most contamination, all contamination. We plead the blood over our hearts right now. We plead the blood over every dark corner, every secret place, every area of compromise, every hidden wound, every unresolved issue. Blood of Jesus, speak. Speak mercy. Speak cleansing. Speak purification. Speak healing. Let that blood do what it was shed to do. Hallelujah. Father, we pray now that you renew a right spirit within us. Not our old spirit of fear and timidity and insecurity and double-mindedness. A right spirit. A spirit that is properly aligned with your spirit. A spirit that is quick to hear your voice and slow to follow the voice of the enemy. A spirit that is sensitive to the things of heaven and insensitive to the corruption of the world. Lord, renew that spirit within us. Give us fresh fire. Give us fresh hunger. Give us fresh thirst. As the deer panted after the water brook, Psalm 42 - 1, so let our hearts pant after you, God. Not after status. Not after comfort. Not after the approval of men. Let the supreme desire of our hearts be you. Let the first thing we think of when we wake up in the morning be your face. Let the last thing on our lips at night be your name. Let our hearts be absolutely, unreservedly consumed with a love for you that does not cool, that does not grow stale, that does not become routine. Lord, keep us burning. Keep us burning for you. Hallelujah. Now, I want to take authority over some specific [music] things in the spirit. I speak to the spirit of confusion and I declare your assignment over these minds is terminated in the name of Jesus Christ. You will not cloud their thinking anymore. You will not make simple things [music] complicated. You will not take the clear voice of God and distort it into noise. Confusion, we bind you and cast you out in the name of Jesus. And Father, release the spirit of wisdom and sound judgment. Release clarity of mind. Let these minds think clearly. Let them hear clearly. Let them discern correctly. Let them make good decisions. Let them no longer be manipulated by confusion but governed by the clarity that comes from above. James 3:17 says, "But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be entreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality and without hypocrisy." Lord, release this wisdom from above over every mind this morning in Jesus' name. Hallelujah. I speak to the spirit of anxiety and worry and I declare you an illegal occupant of these minds. Jesus said in John 14:27, "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you. Not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid." The peace of Jesus Christ is not a feeling, it is a person, and that person lives inside every born-again believer. So, I decree the peace of Christ to arise in the minds and hearts of everyone under this anointing right now. Every anxious thought be silenced. Every fearful projection be canceled. Every negative anticipation be uprooted. Philippians 4:6 and 7, be careful for nothing, but in everything by prayer and supplication with Thanksgiving, let your request be made known unto God. And the peace of God which passeth all understanding shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus. That peace that passes understanding, that supernatural, inexplicable, irrational to the natural mind peace, I decree it over you right now in the name of Jesus Christ. Let it guard your heart. Let it guard your mind. Let it be a shield against every arrow of mental torment. Hallelujah. I speak to the residue of past trauma in the minds of everyone watching. Trauma has a way of rewiring the mind. It has a way of leaving a physiological and psychological and spiritual imprint. And many of you are still processing life through the lens of painful experiences that happened years ago, [music] sometimes decades ago. And I want you to know Jesus is the healer of the brokenhearted. Luke 4:18, he said, "The spirit of the Lord is upon me [music] because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor. He hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised." You that are bruised, you that have been wounded by life, I declare liberty to you this morning. Jesus is healing the bruised places. Jesus is healing the fractured memories. Jesus is touching the places that still hurt when you think about them. Receive healing in your mind right now. Receive healing in your emotions right now. By his stripes you are healed, and that healing includes your inner man, it includes your soul, it includes every dimension of your being that has been broken in Jesus' mighty name. Hallelujah. Father, I pray now that you establish new patterns of thinking in these minds. Romans 12:2 transform them by the renewing of their mind. Let there be a supernatural rewiring happening as a result of this prayer and this word today. Let the patterns that were formed by the world begin to be dismantled and let the patterns of the kingdom take their place. Let them begin to default to faith [music] instead of fear. Let them begin to default to gratitude instead of complaint. Let them begin to default to possibility instead of limitation.
